Hi Jill — great question. High-level options below and I've attached a simple model that walks the math.

Option 1 — Marginal-first (preferred for transparency)
- Customer pays marginal per-token rate at each breakpoint.
- When converting from slab commitments, Redwood offers a short "bridge credit" to offset the delta for the first billing period, then phases down over the next 1-3 months.
- True-up at quarter end to reconcile actual usage vs committed buckets.

Option 2 — Blended transitional rate
- For the first renewal period we can offer a blended effective rate that mixes historical slab pricing with target marginal pricing. Clear clawback if usage drops.

Option 3 — Slab + runway credits
- Keep slab for an initial period and provide runway credits that convert into token credits as usage moves to marginal tiers.

Attached: acme_commit_matrix.xlsx (your file, I added columns for the marginal conversion scenarii). Also attached a short worked example in the sheet '3q-conversion'.

If you like, we can schedule a 30-min math session with finance next week. Recommended: marginal-first + 60–90 day bridge credit for clean invoicing and predictable unit economics.

Best,

Thanks for the draft. Quick notes:

- 12% bridge credit is OK if we attach the following guardrails: 1) amortize over 90 days, 2) quarter-end true-up with tier reset only on the next billing cycle, and 3) a one-quarter clawback if actual usage is <70% of forecast.
- Prefer 'marginal-first' as the customer-facing default; it's easier for their finance team to reconcile and aligns with Redwood's unit-economics playbook.
- Recommend we require a minimum quarterly commit equal to 50% of their trailing 3-month usage to avoid adverse selection.

I've redlined the term sheet with these changes — see acme_term_sheet_v3.pdf (redline). If legal agrees, we should present Option A (marginal-first + 12% 90-day bridge + 50% min) and Option B (blended one-time transitional rate) as fallbacks.

Option A (Recommended) — Marginal-first with bridge
- Marginal per-token ladder with breakpoints at 100M / 300M / 1B tokens
- 12% bridge credit applied month 1 of new term, amortized linearly across 90 days on invoice
- Quarter-end true-up; tiers reset next billing cycle
- Minimum quarterly commit = 50% of trailing 3-month usage (to be listed on the term sheet)

Option B — Blended transitional rate
- One-time blended effective rate for the first quarter, then shift to marginal ladder
- Blended calculation shown in sheet 'Q1-blended' of the attached model

Option C — Slab endurance + runway credits
- Keep current slab bands, provide runway token credits that convert as usage grows; includes 3-month review and manual tier adjustment guardrail
